non_interference_contract.law: MOP owns this machine. Never signal, kill, renice, or inspect MOP's internals. Observe only.
non_interference_contract.identification_method: by cost, not by name -- any python-family process above 20 percent CPU that this campaign did not start. Deliberately over-inclusive: overcounting causes more backoff, which is the safe direction.

forbidden: giant model load or full-model generation

RELIEF_WINDOW.why_not: load/core measured 1.655 against a relief ceiling of 0.70. MOP holds ~21 of 28 cores. No relief window has opened at any point in this campaign.
RELIEF_WINDOW.entry_condition: load/core <= 0.70 sustained across at least 3 samples, plus memory, swap, thermal and disk all green
RELIEF_WINDOW.on_entry: ONE bounded micro-job, which must declare max wall time, max RSS, max threads, max source bytes, rollback and stop trigger BEFORE launch

HEAVY_FORBIDDEN.if_mop_stops: mark HEAVY_WINDOW_AVAILABLE and stop. A human decides what runs. The governor marks it; it never acts on it.

armed: available memory below 10 percent of RAM

deliberately_not_armed.why: MOP's normal working state is load/core ~1.66. Backing off on load alone would mean never running at all, which is paralysis rather than caution. Backoff fires on the conditions a light job can genuinely make worse.

backoff_triggers.action: pause or kill HAWKING light jobs only. Never MOP.

concurrency_decision.why_not_six: delegated lanes run cargo builds, which are real CPU. Six concurrent lanes beside a machine already at 21 of 28 cores would be a measurable regression to MOP. Three is the bounded process count the resource law asks for.
